instructions.question: What emotional attitude does the poster of this Swedish tweet express or imply: positive, neutral, or negative?
instructions.rule: Judge the poster's own attitude, including attitude shown through what they choose to share. Retweets of bad news, criticism, complaints or troubling topics (accidents, layoffs, political attacks, deaths) are negative even when they sound factual. Friendly, helpful, joking or approving replies are positive even when mild. Neutral is for plain information, questions, prices, announcements and news shared with no evident stance, and also for opinions that stay matter-of-fact.

neutral.what: Factual information, news headlines, price updates, questions, event reports and announcements, and opinions stated in a matter-of-fact way without clear emotion.
examples: Nu har vi ändrat priset igen: E85: 9,44 B95: 14,53 Diesel: 14,27 (We have changed the price again)
@powerpuff_ronja vad ska du läsa? (what are you going to study?)
Larm om kraftig smäll i Stockholm - Aftonbladet (Alarm about a loud bang in Stockholm)
neutral.cues: RT of news, links, priser (prices), questions such as vad/hur (what/how), dates and numbers
neutral.not_for: News that the poster frames as bad, or that reports setbacks, is negative, e.g. 'raket exploderade ... :(' (rocket exploded). Neutral-sounding replies that disagree or correct someone are often negative.

positive.what: Joy, praise, congratulations, enthusiasm, friendly or playful replies, humor, welcomes, hope, approval.
examples: @KristerIsaksson Snygg lösning !! (Nice solution!!)
@papperferdinand grattis till ert giftemål det var ett vackert bröllop :,) (congrats on your marriage, it was a beautiful wedding)
@stroemberg en av de bästa burgarna i stan så ja på den! (one of the best burgers in town so yes to it!)
positive.cues: :), <3, haha, grattis (congrats), härligt (lovely), bra (good), gillar (like), välkommen (welcome), hurra (hooray), pepp (excited), älskar (love)
positive.not_for: Fan screaming such as 'VAD FINA NI ÄR ... ORKAR INTE' (HOW PRETTY YOU ARE ... CAN'T COPE) is negative. Missing someone ('Jag saknar er redan', I already miss you) is neutral.

negative.what: Anger, hate, sadness, complaints, insults, cynicism, criticism of politicians or society, disagreement or correction, and sharing bad or troubling news.
examples: Livet e hårt och sen dör man (Life is hard and then you die)
RT @TobiasHoldstock: 3400 uppsagda med regeringens halverade RUT-avdrag ... Sorgligt. (3400 laid off ... Sad.)
@roxanakozlik något riktigt skevt (something really twisted)
negative.cues: hatar (hate), jävla/fan (damn), tråkigt (boring/sad), sorgligt (sad), skevt (twisted), :(, svin (pigs), dumma (stupid), förtryck (oppression), nej (no)
negative.not_for: Swearing used for enthusiasm, such as 'SÅ. JÄVLA. BRA' (SO. DAMN. GOOD) or 'Fyfan vad jag gillar' (damn how I like), is positive. Mild political commentary without clear emotion is neutral.
